overview_markdown:
LettaBot was a personal AI assistant built on the Letta Code SDK, designed to live across Telegram, Slack, Discord, WhatsApp, and Signal with a single unified agent memory. It supported persistent long-term memory across sessions, local tool execution (file reads, code search, shell commands), voice message transcription via OpenAI Whisper, heartbeat check-ins, scheduling, and read-only Bluesky Jetstream feed ingestion. Deployment was streamlined via a Railway template and YAML configuration.

The project is now **officially deprecated and archived**. The maintainers direct all new users to Letta Code's Channels (for messaging integrations), Remote Environments (for always-on VPS agents via outbound WebSocket), and `letta cron` (for scheduling). Existing deployments continue to function, and migration is described as taking roughly 20 minutes.

Compared to OpenClaw, LettaBot offered a polished multi-channel memory-centric experience backed by Letta's agent infrastructure, but it lacked a community skill registry and is no longer maintained. It is best treated as a reference implementation or a migration starting point rather than a viable OpenClaw alternative going forward.
